samples.text:
The graph shows how many visitors came to a seaside town in each month of 2010 and 2020.

In 2010, the number of visitors was low in the beginning of the year, about 11 to 15 thousand from January to March. Then it increased quickly from April and in July it was 90 thousand. The highest month was August with 96 thousand visitors. After August the number decreased very fast to 50 thousand in September and 24 thousand in October, and it was only 13 and 14 thousand in November and December.

In 2020 the pattern was similar, but the numbers in summer was much lower. The highest was also August but only 65 thousand, and July was 60 thousand. However, in the winter months there were more visitors than in 2010. For example, January had 18 thousand and December had 28 thousand. October also was higher, 35 thousand compare to 24 thousand in 2010.

Overall, summer was the most popular time in both years, but in 2020 the visitors were more spread in the year.
samples.why: Overview present but placed late · key comparison covered though detail is somewhat listed · adequate vocabulary · errors in agreement, word order and word form that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The line graph compares the number of people who visited a seaside town each month in 2010 with the number in 2020.

Overall, the town was most popular in the summer months in both years, with August being the busiest month. However, the seasonal variation was far less extreme in 2020, as the town attracted fewer visitors in summer but more during the rest of the year.

In 2010, visitor numbers were very low at the start of the year, ranging from 11,000 to 15,000 between January and March. They then rose sharply, reaching 90,000 in July and peaking at 96,000 in August. After this, the figure dropped dramatically to 24,000 in October before falling further to 13,000 and 14,000 in the last two months.

The 2020 figures followed the same general trend but in a much flatter form. The peak in August was only 65,000, around 31,000 fewer than in 2010, and the July figure was 60,000. On the other hand, the off-season months were busier: for instance, January attracted 18,000 visitors, and October and December had 35,000 and 28,000 respectively, both clearly higher than a decade ago.
samples.why: Clear overview of shared seasonality and flatter 2020 pattern · key features and differences highlighted · good cohesion · appropriate vocabulary · mostly accurate grammar with a slight tense inconsistency.

samples.text:
The graph compares monthly visitor numbers to a seaside town in 2010 and 2020.

In both years, tourism was heavily concentrated in the summer, with August the peak month. The key difference, however, is that the seasonal pattern became much less pronounced over the decade: summer numbers fell substantially, while the quieter months attracted more visitors.

In 2010, the town received between 11,000 and 15,000 visitors a month during the first quarter. Numbers then rose steeply from April, reaching 90,000 in July and a peak of 96,000 in August, roughly nine times the February low. This was followed by an equally steep decline to 24,000 in October and just 13,000 in November.

By 2020, the summer surge had become far more modest. August remained the busiest month, but with only 65,000 visitors, while July saw 60,000, some 30,000 fewer than a decade earlier. Conversely, arrivals outside the peak season were consistently higher. January and February brought in 18,000 and 17,000 visitors respectively, and the figures for October and December, at 35,000 and 28,000, far exceeded their 2010 equivalents. Only in September were the two years broadly similar, at 50,000 and 48,000.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected, including the flattening of the seasonal curve · clear overview · accurate, well-chosen comparisons · precise, flexible vocabulary · wide range of structures with no errors.
